scope: Native app notification bookkeeping; release and development builds
behavior: Completion deduplication identifiers stay in memory, bounded by current snapshot transfer IDs.
Engine instance changes reset bookkeeping and establish a completion baseline without notification submission.
Normal snapshots remove the legacy completedTorrents preferences key without loading its identifiers.
Development activity clearing removes the legacy key even while offline and clears in-memory bookkeeping.
Preview and fixture snapshots do not mutate notification preferences or submit notifications.
Activity clearing suppresses notification submission while in progress.

compilerChecks.method: Swift type-check, arm64 macOS 15; no app execution

limitations: An offline launch without a snapshot or explicit clear leaves the legacy key untouched.
Notification Center records, backups and older application versions have separate retention.
No private-session, automatic-expiry or secure-erasure claim.
pending: Transfer removal/re-addition and bounded identifier lifetime
Offline clearing and completion during clearing
Legacy preferences cleanup in the correct app domain
